bones.name: tooth_canine_11_23
bones.function: One of the four canine teeth (dentes canini), placed laterally to each lateral incisor. Larger and stronger than the incisors, its large conical crown tapers to a blunted point or cusp that projects beyond the level of the other teeth, and its long single root sinks deeply into the bone, causing a well-marked prominence upon the surface of the jaw. The upper canines are larger and longer than the lower and usually present a distinct basal ridge.
bones.source: grays1918:larger and longer than the lower, and usually present a distinct basal ridge
bones.note: Popularly called an eye tooth; in occlusion it rests partly on the lower canine and partly on the first premolar. Each tooth consists of a crown projecting above the gum, a root imbedded in the alveolus, and a constricted neck between them.

bones.name: tooth_incisor_10_22
bones.function: One of the eight incisors (dentes incisivi), the four front teeth of each dental arch, named for their sharp chisel-shaped cutting edge adapted for biting food. The crown is convex and polished on its labial surface, concave on its lingual surface, and the single conical root is transversely flattened and anchored in its alveolar socket. The upper incisors are larger and stronger than the lower and are directed obliquely downward and forward; the central ones are larger than the lateral.
bones.source: grays1918:larger and stronger than the lower, and are directed obliquely downward and forward
bones.note: On upper incisors the lingual surface often bears an inverted V-shaped eminence near the gum, the basal ridge or cingulum; the cingulum is absent on the lowers. Each tooth consists of a crown projecting above the gum, a root imbedded in the alveolus, and a constricted neck between them.

bones.name: tooth_molar_14_26
bones.function: One of the twelve molar teeth (dentes molares), the largest of the permanent set, whose broad, nearly cubical crowns surmounted by four or five cusps are adapted for grinding and pounding food. Three molars stand posterior to each second premolar in each half-arch. Each upper molar has three roots, two buccal and one diverging lingual; as a rule the first is the largest and the third the smallest of the upper molars.
bones.source: grays1918:Each upper molar has three roots
bones.note: As a rule the first upper molar is the largest of the upper molars, its crown usually bearing four tubercles. Each tooth consists of a crown projecting above the gum, a root imbedded in the alveolus, and a constricted neck between them.
